findings.name: \"Words\" search mode finds nothing when the words are split between the issue title and its body

The same words match when they are not split: \"verifies published\" (both in one issue body) returns #2, \"ownership proposal\" returns #4, \"captain merging\" returns #4. Also tried \"clarify verifies\" (title word of #2 + body word of #2) and \"rotation proposal\" (body word of #4 + title word of #4): both return \"No results\". (on /issues)
findings.expected: Issue #2 \"Clarify release ownership\" is listed, because it contains both words — \"ownership\" in its title and \"verifies\" in its body (\"Document who coordinates a release and who verifies the published tag.\").
findings.actual: The page shows \"No results / Try adjusting your search filters.\" and 0 results. The same words match when they are not split: \"verifies published\" (both in one issue body) returns #2, \"ownership proposal\" returns #4, \"captain merging\" returns #4. Also tried \"clarify verifies\" (title word of #2 + body word of #2) and \"rotation proposal\" (body word of #4 + title word of #4): both return \"No results\".
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open https://5503-ioyiuw0ebjuremypnxaoz.e2b.app/issues?q=verifies&state=open&search_mode=words — the one-word search "verifies" lists eval/harbor-handbook#2 "Clarify release ownership", whose body contains "who verifies the published tag".
Change the query to ownership verifies, keep the search mode on "Words", submit.
The page shows "No results" ("Try adjusting your search filters."), although #2 contains "ownership" in its title and "verifies" in its body.
Same for q=clarify+verifies&search_mode=words (#2 title + #2 body) and q=rotation+proposal&search_mode=words (#4 body + #4 title): both show "No results".

findings.name: Escape does not close the Assignees picker once a person has been ticked
findings.summary: After a user has been clicked in the picker, Escape does nothing: the picker stays open (with the tick marks) and repeated Escape presses do not close it. Escape only works if no user was clicked yet. Because the choice is only applied when the picker loses focus, a person who ticks a user and then presses Escape expecting to cancel or close is left with the picker open and a pending, unsaved change. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/4)
findings.expected: Escape closes the assignee picker, as it closes the other dropdowns and dialogs of the app; the picker is a listbox that captures the keyboard, so Escape is the normal way out without a mouse.
findings.actual: After a user has been clicked in the picker, Escape does nothing: the picker stays open (with the tick marks) and repeated Escape presses do not close it. Escape only works if no user was clicked yet. Because the choice is only applied when the picker loses focus, a person who ticks a user and then presses Escape expecting to cancel or close is left with the picker open and a pending, unsaved change.
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/4 and sign in as eval if needed.
In the right sidebar click "Assignees" (the gear row) to open the assignee picker.
Click the user "maya" in the picker so that her row gets a tick.
Press the Escape key.
Look at the picker: it is still open; press Escape a second time and it is still open. The same happens on issue #2 and while the picker's "Filter Assignee" box contains text after a tick.
Only a click somewhere else on the page closes the picker.

findings.name: Tick in the Assignees picker is saved only when the picker is closed by clicking elsewhere; reloading loses it
findings.summary: The tick is only a pending state: no request is sent when the user is clicked (the network shows the assignee POST only later, when the picker is closed by clicking elsewhere). If the person reloads, navigates or leaves the page while the picker is still open, the change is silently lost: the picked user never appears in the "Assignees" sidebar, the issue list shows no avatar for them and the "Assignee" filter does not find the issue for that user. Ticking maya on issue #1 and on issue #4 and then reloading left both issues with alex only, and filtering /issues by maya still lists only issue #9. (on /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/4)
findings.expected: A ticked user is saved (or the picker says "not saved yet") so that reloading the page shows the user in the sidebar Assignees and in the issue list avatars; the POST is sent as soon as the user is picked, as it is for labels, milestone and the other sidebar pickers.
findings.actual: The tick is only a pending state: no request is sent when the user is clicked (the network shows the assignee POST only later, when the picker is closed by clicking elsewhere). If the person reloads, navigates or leaves the page while the picker is still open, the change is silently lost: the picked user never appears in the "Assignees" sidebar, the issue list shows no avatar for them and the "Assignee" filter does not find the issue for that user. Ticking maya on issue #1 and on issue #4 and then reloading left both issues with alex only, and filtering /issues by maya still lists only issue #9.
reproSteps: Open /eval/harbor-handbook/issues/4 (signed in as eval; issue already has assignee alex).
In the right sidebar click "Assignees" to open the picker.
Click the user "maya": her row gets a tick next to alex's tick, and the sidebar/list are still covered by the picker.
Without clicking anywhere else, reload the page (F5).
The reloaded issue shows only alex under Assignees; maya is not assigned. The same happened on issue #1: tick maya, reload, only alex remains.
Check /issues?type=all&state=open&assignee=3 (maya): only issue #9 is listed, so neither #1 nor #4 got maya.

findings.name: Issue tracker settings accept an invalid regular expression in the external number format and report success
findings.summary: The settings are saved: the green banner \"The repository settings have been updated.\" appears and after a reload the Regular Expression radio is still selected with \"(\" in the \"Regular Expression Pattern\" field. No error is shown anywhere, so the number format is silently broken. (In the same form an empty or non-http URL is refused: \"The external issue tracker URL is not a valid URL.\") (on /eval/harbor-handbook/settings)
findings.expected: The form should refuse a pattern that is not a valid regular expression, with a message next to the field, the way it refuses an invalid External Issue Tracker URL in the same form, instead of reporting the settings as updated.
findings.actual: The settings are saved: the green banner \"The repository settings have been updated.\" appears and after a reload the Regular Expression radio is still selected with \"(\" in the \"Regular Expression Pattern\" field. No error is shown anywhere, so the number format is silently broken. (In the same form an empty or non-http URL is refused: \"The external issue tracker URL is not a valid URL.\")
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, open /eval/harbor-handbook/settings and scroll to Advanced Settings.
Select the "Use External Issue Tracker" radio and put any valid URL in "External Issue Tracker URL" (I used https://example.org/issues).
Under "External Issue Tracker Number Format" select "Regular Expression (ISSUE-\d+) , ISSUE-(\d+)".
Type a pattern that is not a valid regular expression, a single "(" , into "Regular Expression Pattern".
Click the Update Settings button of the Advanced Settings section.
The page answers "The repository settings have been updated." ; after a reload the Regex radio is still selected and the field still contains "(".
